title: Over the shoulder
logline: Wednesday. The last of the arc. Wood drawing at the table and, for the first time in the strip, the panel is drawn from behind him — over his shoulder — as if someone were looking. The strip's first awareness that someone is.

panels.composition: The garage, from behind WOOD's shoulder: the table, the pad, his hand, the pen. The reader's viewpoint, for the first time, is someone standing behind him.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a view over a man's shoulder from behind showing his hand drawing on a pad at a drafting table, as if someone stood behind him
image.notes: The over-the-shoulder viewpoint: first use. It returns in Run 7's From Behind.

panels.composition: The pad, from that angle: the strip he's drawing is this one. Panel one: a man from behind.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up over a shoulder of a pad where the panel being drawn shows a man seen from behind at a table

panels.composition: Wood's head turning, slightly. Not all the way. The dog, on the floor, looking straight at the reader.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, over a man's shoulder, his head turning slightly, an old dog on the floor looking directly at the viewer, no words

panels.composition: The garage from the door, normal. Wood at the table, back turned. Nobody behind him. The three drawings on the wall. The fourth face-down. Held.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a garage studio from its doorway with a man at a drafting table with his back turned and nobody behind him, three drawings on the wall, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: The over-the-shoulder panel. Someone is looking. Nobody's there.
